source.title: Understanding the unstable convergence of gradient descent
source.authors: Kwangjun Ahn; J. Zhang; Suvrit Sra

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own CIFAR-10 training experiments on how gradient descent behaves above the stability threshold, using loss and relative-progress measurements rather than testing the listed convergence recipes directly.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own CIFAR-10 experiments with GD and SGD. Results cited from Cohen et al. and other prior work are not recorded as this study’s results. The paper reports training accuracy reaching 95% as the stopping point for Experiments 2 and 3, but does not report final training classification error for the wider CIFAR-10 experiments.
record.test_reason: The study explicitly follows Cohen et al.'s CIFAR-10 full-batch GD setup and reports its own training-loss and sharpness trajectories bearing on V5. Its additional relative-progress analysis explains those results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors characterize unstable convergence through long-run non-monotonic loss decrease, oscillatory updates and relative progress near zero. They propose lack of sufficiently flat stationary points and forward-invariant regions as explanations, and derive conditional links to sharpness. They do not establish a universal convergence guarantee or the complete squared-loss catapult mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Uses full-batch GD and minibatch SGD on CIFAR-10 with cross-entropy to study unstable convergence, loss and relative progress; does not reproduce the squared-loss catapult recipe or test the listed initialization, shortcut, width, or normalization conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Behavior differs with activation: linear networks diverge while tanh and ReLU networks converge in the reported unstable setting. A sufficiently large rate can also diverge (η = 2/10).

fits_no_version.finding: Stable-regime relative progress remains negative and loss decreases monotonically.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stable full-batch GD has different relative-progress behavior from unstable GD.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative progress agrees with an expression involving directional smoothness, including in minibatch SGD experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directional smoothness approximately predicts relative progress along the tested training trajectories.

fits_no_version.finding: Minibatch SGD decreases training loss over time although expected relative progress is nonnegative for most measured iterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Realized long-run SGD loss decrease can coexist with nonnegative estimated one-step expected loss change.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 162, 2022
record.problems: CIFAR-10 training classification error is not reported as an outcome; most detailed plots provide no exact tabulated values. Selected experiments stop when training accuracy reaches 95%, and exact step sizes are omitted for some comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for plots checking the directional-smoothness identity (Experiments 4–5) or SGD identity comparisons (Experiments 8–9) beyond the summarized text outcomes; those do not directly report training error or recovery of loss. Cited studies’ results are excluded.

untested.parts: No test of near-zero classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks. Experiments use fully connected networks; 95% training accuracy is a stopping rule, not evidence about eventual interpolation. CIFAR-100 and corrupted labels are untested.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons are untested.
Depth degradation in plain convolutional networks and comparisons with identity shortcuts or special initialization are untested.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth are untested.

The squared-loss catapult sequence relative to the initial linearized model, including a brief initial loss rise followed by curvature reduction, is untested. Divergence from an initially subthreshold rate is not established. Section 4.4 provides conditional reasoning about sharpness saturation, not a general empirical demonstration across settings.
No normalization-versus-no-normalization training-speed or learning-rate comparison, and no Fixup comparison.

missing.what: The study's own paired ReLU training-loss and sharpness trajectories, showing loss decrease despite failure of the stability condition. Distinguish the displayed trajectory from claims attributed to Cohen et al.
missing.locator: Figure 1 and its caption; Sections 1 and 3.1

missing.what: Separate loss-trajectory results for the two- and four-hidden-layer ReLU networks. R7 captures only the diagnostic relation and omits the loss results relevant to unstable convergence.
missing.locator: Section 4.3.1, Experiment 6, both sets of plots

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source listed for V5. Cross-entropy experiments extend the tested setting; that difference alone is not a scope limitation. Neither the linear control's divergence nor the explicitly excessive-rate divergence warrants a challenges verdict. No files or external sources were accessed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, SGD/Adam comparisons, model size, early stopping, or regularized recipes; CIFAR-10 training classification error is not reported as a result.

Does not test squared loss, a sweep over rates relative to the initial linearized model’s stability limit, or sharpness hovering over long training; its reported CIFAR-10 results use cross-entropy and compare selected step sizes.
